saints.dates: First century; exact episcopal dates and death circumstances not established here

summary.text: St. Linus is named in the New Testament and remembered in Orthodox tradition as an early bishop of Rome after the Apostles.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: The final greeting of Second Timothy includes Linus among Christians sending greetings. The verse supplies his name but does not provide a childhood, conversion story or detailed account of his ministry. Later identification with the bishop of Rome comes from the Church’s historical tradition.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: St. Irenaeus, writing in the second century, says that the Apostles entrusted the episcopal office of the Church at Rome to St. Linus. He explicitly identifies him with the Linus mentioned in the letters to Timothy. This is the source used when the lesson discusses the public succession of teachers and bishops.
blocks.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

blocks.text: The cited OCA entry identifies his episcopal succession but does not describe his death. The account of martyrdom in the same group entry belongs to a different member of that group and must not be transferred to Linus. No execution method or exact death year is asserted here.

blocks.text: The OCA commemorates St. Linus on November 5 with other Apostles of the Seventy and names him a successor of St. Peter at Rome. The early witness concerns continuity of apostolic teaching and ministry; a one-sentence notice should not be expanded into an invented biography.
